(1) The popliteal lymph-node enlargement in the rat GVH reaction is due mainly to proliferation of lymphocytes, both T and B. (2) The lymphocyte proliferation is initiated on the third day after transfer of spleen cells and reaches a peak on the seventh day.
the lymph node enlargement during the GVH reaction is due to cell proliferation and that the majority of proliferating cells are T lymphocytes.

the cellular composition of lymphoid organs in the rat during a GVH reaction.
the cellular composition of the poplitea lymph node in the GVH reaction.
the cellular composition of the poplite al lymph node during the graft-versus-host reaction.

the GVH reaction in the popliteal node is an immunological response in which lymphocytes are the main cellular components and proliferation of cells is the central mechanism.

the popliteal node GVH response involves a massive proliferation of cells of both T- and B-cell lineage.

the popliteal node graft-versus-Host reaction is a model of lymphoid hyperplasia in which the cellular composition of the node is well known and in which cell proliferation can be quantified.
